headline: Unprecedented drop in French students' performance echoes worldwide decline
description: Reading and maths scores for 15-year-olds in France have fallen to their lowest levels since 2000, mirroring trends seen in comparable countries. Among the reasons cited to explain this global phenomenon are attitudes toward learning, the role of digital technology, the lasting effects of the Covid-19 crisis and a lack of parental involvement. In France, significant social and gender inequalities persist.

headline: Mistral AI raises €3 billion in response to doubts over its strategic direction
description: The French artificial intelligence start-up, accused by some experts of having abandoned the race against its American and Chinese rivals to focus on data centers and services, insists it has not given up on producing cutting-edge models. It has secured its largest-ever funding round and welcomed Samsung as a shareholder.

headline: Thousands of 'Greater Serbia' supporters attend funeral of Ratko Mladic in Belgrade
description: The former commander of the Serbian army in Bosnia and Herzegovina, who was convicted by an international court for genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity during the conflicts in the former Yugoslavia in the 1990s and who died in prison in The Hague, was buried in the Serbian capital on Monday.

In this French city, social diversity in schools has almost disappeared
description: According to studies, the southern city of Perpignan is the most educationally segregated in France. It's divided between private schools, which rank among the most privileged in the country, and public schools, which, in almost every case, sit at the exact opposite end of the social scale.

headline: Annie Ernaux's words resonate among new generation of women: 'She doesn't try to make it poetic'
description: Annie Ernaux's books, which delve into the intimate side of the female experience, have found unprecedented resonance among women. The work of the Nobel laureate in literature echoed through the voices of two actresses – Tess Barthélemy in a film directed by her mother, Judith Godrèche, and Suzanne de Baecque in a solo stage performance – as well as in the powerful readings by high school girls in a documentary by Claire Simon.
